discovery: Theory of collective motion and flocking in active matter

nominees.name: Yuhai Tu
nominees.affiliation: IBM T. J. Watson Research Center, USA

subfield: Statistical physics / soft and active matter
motivation: Vicsek's 1995 minimal model of self-propelled particles showed that simple local alignment rules produce a nonequilibrium phase transition to collective motion. Toner and Tu then built a hydrodynamic field theory of flocks. Using renormalization-group arguments, they showed that active systems can sustain true long-range orientational order in two dimensions, which the Mermin-Wagner theorem forbids at equilibrium. They also predicted giant number fluctuations and anomalous sound modes. These results founded active matter as a branch of statistical physics. Through extensive simulation and coarse-grained theory, the work turned a messy many-body problem, the coordinated motion of birds, bacteria, cells and synthetic colloids, into a clear physical picture. It has since been confirmed in experiments on bacterial suspensions, motility assays, epithelial tissues and Quincke rollers. Its concepts now shape research across physics, biology and materials science, reaching far beyond their origin.
